Probably not. Although the Moon is geometrically above the horizon, it is only **11.4% illuminated** and lies just **39.4° from the Sun** in a bright daytime sky. At **18.2° altitude**, atmospheric haze and extinction further reduce its already low contrast.

Under exceptionally transparent conditions, an experienced observer who knows the exact position might possibly glimpse the thin waning crescent, especially using binoculars first. But for an ordinary unaided observer who only knows roughly where to look, it would most likely be **effectively invisible**.

So while the Moon is technically up, you can reasonably expect **not to see it**. Avoid sweeping near the Sun with binoculars or a telescope.
